intent: Trace the reported global smallpox case count over the years from 1920 through 1980 to determine how the number changed across that period.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
How did the reported global smallpox case count change from 1920 through 1980?

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The reported global smallpox case count declined overall from 400,000 cases in 1920 to 20,000 cases in 1980, despite intermediate fluctuations.
units.computation: Compare first value (400000 at 1920) to last value (20000 at 1980); note intermediate values 120000 at 1940 and 270000 at 1960 to show non-monotonic decline.
accept: States that reported global smallpox cases decreased from 1920 to 1980.
Mentions the start value 400,000 and end value 20,000.
Describes an overall downward trend with fluctuations.
reject: Claims cases increased overall from 1920 to 1980.
Describes only a single intermediate point without the overall change.

optional_valid: Mentions the peak of 620,000 cases at point_order 15.
Notes that the lowest value is 20,000 cases at 1980.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the decline (e.g., vaccination campaigns) not present in the table.
Exact year-by-year values for all 31 points.
Claims about other diseases or regions.
review_notes: The table summary lists only four x-anchored rows plus two rows with empty x; the trend unit uses the four anchored rows to prove the overall change.
Intermediate fluctuations are represented by the 1940 and 1960 values, which are sufficient to show non-monotonicity without listing every point.
